Every dictation made with the owner's Super+Alt+D toggle is cleaned by a small local CPU model (S1-mini by Superwhisper) before it lands in the clipboard, with no server or service the owner has to install, start or maintain. The model is loaded only when a dictation needs it and is unloaded after Handy's existing idle timeout, so it holds no memory when unused. Quill or any second model entry; per-shortcut presets; streaming output; GPU/Vulkan inference; linking llama.cpp into the Handy process; changes to speech transcription; upstream PR. Binary location: `/usr/lib/Handy/llm/llama-server` (not `/usr/bin`, to avoid clashing with Fedora's `llama-cpp` package). Resolution order: env `HANDY_LLAMA_SERVER` (dev only), then `/usr/lib/Handy/llm/llama-server`. A missing binary is a `LocalLlmError::BinaryMissing`, never a panic. It is built statically (`-DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF`, CPU backend only) so it shares no libraries with Handy's bundled ggml. `ModelEntry { id, display_name, attribution, card_url, backend: BackendKind::LlamaServer, file_name, url (Hugging Face resolve URL at a pinned
